items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: I remember one of the associates in our dance orchestra very well. His name was -- his name was Phil Lambert

ctx.x: Well, I wanted to play all of them. Our family had a feeling, it seemed, for music, and we could acquire a capability of playing any type of music. I tried everything from symphony to concert to jazz, all those music. It seemed very easy for me to acquire the feeling, and so by the time I was into high school, I was playing all of these different types of music fairly well. Of course, I was continually in the school bands, the school orchestras, and I had even gotten so I could play in the school dance band,…
Now, by this time I'm over in San Francisco, and I remember one of the associates in our dance orchestra very well. His name was -- his name was Phil Lambert, and later -- many

years later I ran into Phil Lambert, and he was the director of the pit orchestra at the Fox Theater in Washington, D. C., and he told me he was going from there into New York into some orchestra, but I never saw him any more. But by this time I was thoroughly interested, and trombone was my instrument.
